To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the exponent of the degree distribution of the resulting graph is given by 1 + alpha, where alpha = 1 - (2 - gamma)/gamma, gamma is the parameter of the duplication model.
the exponent of power-law graphs is determined by the duplication process, that partial duplication can lead to exponents less than two, and that the starting graph does not matter.
the exponent of the degree distribution for a power-law graph is a monotonic function of the probability of duplication and the number of nodes duplicated.

the duplication models are the only models that can explain the observed power-law exponents of biological networks, and the observed exponents are consistent with the assumption that biological networks are evolved by a duplication process.
duplication models are not just a toy model for the growth of complex networks, but they can be used to explain the power-law exponents of biological networks.

biological networks are not fundamentally different from other complex networks.
